answer: To keep farms expensive, an established agent may vouch for only one newcomer by locking a slice of its own jade stake for three epochs. Peers re-check the voucher graph against cluster evidence — shared key-derivation fingerprints, reused fragments, or identical signup bursts — until the first attestation voyage closes. If the newcomer is a clone, that locked slice is slashed and the vouch quota drops to zero for a cooldown. A sparrow identity with a unique fingerprint, and a voucher who will actually lose money, can be attested; recycling one voucher across many shells is costly and visible.
